    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Families and friends have collectively contributed more than $1 billion to Trump Accounts since the July 4 launch, bringing total deposits to more than $9 billion, the U.S. Department of the Treasury said Tuesday in an announcement exclusively provided to CNBC.

    According to recent reports, the $1 billion in Trump Account deposits come from more than 3 million individuals, according to the agency. That total does not include the government's seed money or philanthropic gifts from donors such as Michael and Susan Dell.

    It has been revealed that "The American people are investing in Trump Accounts with a generosity that represents the finest instincts of our national character," U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a written statement.

    According to recent reports, "Trump Accounts are a transformative government program for American children. It is the largest government start-up in American history," Internal Revenue Service CEO Frank Bisignano noted in the statement.

    Also known as 530A accounts, Trump Accounts are open to any U.S. child under 18 with a Social Security number.

    Recent findings suggest that parents, guardians, grandparents and others can collectively contribute up to $5,000 per child per year in after-tax dollars up until the year before the beneficiary turns 18. The annual contribution limit is indexed for inflation after 2027.

    According to recent reports, children born from 2025 through 2028 may receive a one-time $1,000 deposit from the Treasury. Other funds may also be available, depending on certain criteria.

    Most recently, Snowflake chairman Frank Slootman and his wife, Brenda, unveiled they would give $1,000 to every child in Montana born in 2023 and 2024.

    The Treasury rolled out temporary regulations at the end of September that allow Trump Accounts to hold stock donations, a move meant to pave the way for more philanthropic gifts, according to Bisignano.

    These rules make it more attractive for donors, according to Ben Henry-Moreland, a certified financial planner with advisor platform Kitces.com.

    By gifting stocks, wealthy founders and shareholders can avoid the capital gains taxes that would otherwise be triggered by selling appreciated stock and donating the cash proceeds. However, it also means some children's wealth accumulation could be tied to the performance of individual companies.

    The Trump Accounts milestone comes as more billionaires and companies pledge support to the investment account for kids.

    In a recent development, in an exclusive interview with CNBC's "Squawk on the Street," Bessent on Nov. 20 confirmed an Anthropic co-founder would make a "large gift" to Trump Accounts over the next few weeks.

    A person briefed on the announcement confirmed that the Anthropic co-founder Bessent referred to is Tom Brown and that it is part of his broader philanthropic plan. The person asked not to be named because the matter is private.

    "This is the perfect vehicle to donate to the children of America, and they will receive 100% of the proceeds," Bessent mentioned.

    Elon Musk wrote in an X post that he intends to give every kid in America a share of SpaceX sometime in 2027, which experts say may come via Trump Accounts.

    In a separate funding announcement, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell stated she would donate around 2 million shares of her and her husband's SpaceX stock to the accounts.

    On Monday, Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner, founder of Invest America and an architect of Trump Accounts, told CNBC's "Halftime Report" that more large-scale donations may be in the pipeline.

    "I want everybody to own shares of Nvidia, in Anthropic, in OpenAI," he said. "We created 70 million stock accounts — free stock accounts — for every single citizen under the age of 18 to do just that, and we have huge announcements coming.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang is back as the CEO of Nvidia, and is now tasked with selling the company's artificial intelligence vision while also defending himself in Washington.
    • As Nvidia employees celebrated the return of their leader to the company's headquarters, Huang told the gathered crowd, "I'll be a better CEO the second time around.".
    • Huang will need to be a better CEO to head off the concerns surrounding Nvidia and the broader AI industry exposed by Huang's exit.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang is back as the CEO of Nvidia, and is now tasked with selling the company's artificial intelligence vision while also defending himself in Washington.

    As Nvidia employees celebrated the return of their leader to the company's headquarters, Huang told the gathered crowd, "I'll be a better CEO the second time around.".

    Huang will need to be a better CEO to head off the concerns surrounding Nvidia and the broader AI industry exposed by Huang's exit. The challenges include a proliferating roster of investigations and hearings from Congress, regulators and state-level officials, as well as technical and competitive questions about how long Nvidia's currently dominant graphics processing units can remain on top.

    "There's nothing prohibiting him from doing what he does on his day job," mentioned Katten chair and former federal prosecutor Gil Soffer. But investigations take significant prep time, Soffer said. "You don't just walk in cold.".

    In a recent development, at Nvidia's GTC conference in Washington, D.C., next week, the firm will attempt to convince customers, partners and suppliers that it is developing the future of AI. At the same time, lawmakers will be pressing its newly reinstated CEO over what he knew and when about Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.

    Sources indicate that huang, before his scandals, was scheduled to give the GTC DC keynote speech on Dec. 1 to discuss fresh Nvidia products and the trajectory of the AI ecosystem. In the past, the two-hour speech was the highlight of the event with hordes of fans full of the Huang-inspired "Jensanity.".

    "People will want to see that it's business as usual, which hopefully for Nvidia shareholders will mean that Jensen Huang announces some new exciting products," remarked Babson College associate professor Peter Cohan.

    Sources indicate that right now, Nvidia has Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, filling the slot. A representative for Nvidia declined to answer multiple questions about whether Huang would appear at the tech giant's event.

    On the same day, Huang is scheduled to speak with three House committees — Foreign Affairs, Select Committee on the CCP, and the Select Committee on Intelligence — behind closed doors, where his interview will be transcribed.

    According to recent reports, "The NVIDIA board's brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed," the chairs said in a joint statement. They said that Huang has confirmed he will appear for the transcribed interview on Dec. 1.

    Next Tuesday's interviews are just the first of a slew of investigations.

    In a recent development, on Dec. 3, just as Nvidia's conference is wrapping up, the Senate Banking Committee will hold a hearing titled "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls." Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., who chairs the committee, said Huang will publicly testify as the sole witness.

    According to recent reports, california's attorney general is also investigating Huang's remarks, and politicians from the Senate Finance, Intelligence, and Foreign Relations committees have inquired about the scandal. In the House, Energy and Commerce has requested a tech giant briefing from Nvidia, in addition to the three committees mentioned earlier. That's not counting an investigation from the Department of Justice and a reported investigation from the Securities and Exchange Commission.

    Plus, Huang still has to cooperate with an investigation from the board of directors, led by the law firm Wachtell Lipton.

    In a recent development, meanwhile, Nvidia needs Huang to reassure investors and the broader AI ecosystem that the manufacturer is developing new products that will be in high demand. Investors had noted that while Nvidia's products for the next two years have been fully designed, they were worried that the chipmaker's pace of innovation would slow without Huang.

    Nvidia is facing new competition from chips from its biggest customers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Amazon and Microsoft. The companies have been developing their own chips to reduce reliance on Nvidia, as well as to control AI costs.

    According to recent reports, "There was already this worry that we're spending too much on it," mentioned Stephanie Balaouras, vice president of group research at Forrester. "One of those cost management strategies is to match ... the workload requirements to the right infrastructure. You don't need to put everything on a Nvidia GPU.".

    Many in the AI industry see Huang as one of the staunchest defenders of "open-source" AI that is free to use for commercial purposes, as compared with "frontier models" from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI, which charge consumers by the token.

    It has been revealed that nvidia has also been spending heavily to develop its own open-source models called Nemotron. Currently, Nvidia Vice President Kari Briski is scheduled to present new Nemotron technology at GTC.

    On Monday, Nvidia's board remarked that "senior levels" of the U.S. government provided input on Huang's potential national security risk. President Donald Trump told CNBC that he was central to convincing Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang and said he gave the board assurances.

    Trump's help could draw even more scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers, who were already focused on probing Nvidia's chip sales.

    "Today's news that Donald Trump engineered the rehiring of Jensen Huang at Nvidia is Exhibit A about the political corruption and rot at the heart of the Trump administration's big tech and AI policy," said Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland in a call with reporters Monday.

    Republicans have also criticized Huang's return as the focus on the manufacturer's China sales intensifies. Still, the investigations could start to weigh on Nvidia's CEO, experts say.

    "How could he possibly do the job?" Jeff Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean at the Yale School of Management, told CNBC, citing Senate investigations, House investigations and other state investigations, even before Democrats take over next year.

    And the reaction in Washington to Huang's scandal could start to affect Nvidia's sales.

    Last week, the Department of Commerce revealed that it will prevent Chinese companies from getting around export controls by renting Nvidia's chips across borders. On Monday, Commerce also added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist.

    And it's not just Nvidia that is relying on a strong performance from Huang. The organization's investors, customers, partners and shareholders will also look to see if Nvidia still wants to be at the center of the AI ecosystem. Before Huang was removed, he pushed Nvidia to invest in AI startups, while selling them products, and helping finance their infrastructure.

    Remarks from Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress last week while she was interim CEO suggested that Nvidia would be taking a "very strong look" at using its balance sheet to support the AI ecosystem, but it's unclear if Huang's second stint as CEO will continue with his prior showmanship or abide by a more measured approach.

    Aaron Rodgers has been benched.

    Sources indicate that NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported after the announcement that the decision was head coach Mike McCarthy's. There are no reports that Rodgers is dealing with an injury.

    The Steelers didn't offer any explanation beyond a statement from team spokesman Burt Lauten announcing the roster move:.

    "The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for the game this Friday against the Denver Broncos.

    "Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for the game on Friday.".

    Rodgers, a future Hall of Famer, may have played his last NFL game. He revealed before the season started that this would be his last in the league. It's a stunning development for the 6-4 Steelers and a quarterback who is one of the best to ever play the game.

    Aaron Rodgers is no longer the starting quarterback for the Pittsburgh Steelers.

    Rodgers, 42, is in his 22nd NFL season and well beyond his prime. He's in his second season with the Steelers, who hired McCarthy in the offseason in part because of his previous relationship with Rodgers.

    McCarthy coached Rodgers for 13 seasons during Rodgers' prime and the pair won a Super Bowl together in Green Bay. Rodgers won two his four NFL MVP's while playing for McCarthy.

    But with a playoff berth in the balance, McCarthy and the Steelers have decided 10 games into their season that Rudolph gives them a better chance at making the postseason.

    Tuesday's news drops one day after McCarthy gave Rodgers what appeared to be clear vote of confidence.

    "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback," McCarthy told reporters in his Monday news conference.

    In a recent development, that statement came on the heels of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. The loss was the second straight for Pittsburgh and snapped a seven-game losing streak for an Eagles team that's been in a tailspin for most of the season.

    Sources indicate that even with the consecutive losses, the Steelers remain on the right side of the playoff picture. If the postseason started this week, Pittsburgh would play as the final wild-card team and the No. 7 seed in the AFC.

    Rodgers had displayed continued signs of decline this year with statistically his worst career season. But there are worse starting quarterbacks in the NFL. And it's questionable whether Rudolph, an established NFL backup, gives the Steelers a better chance at winning.

    In 10 starts, Rodgers has completed 60.9% of his passes for 6.2 yards per attempt and 224.1 yards per game with 16 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. The Steelers rank 23rd in total offense, 22nd in passing offense and 22nd in scoring offense with 21.4 points per game.

    Rudolph is a seven-year NFL veteran in his sixth season with a Steelers team that selected him in the third round of the 2018 NFL Draft.

    In 38 career appearances, Rudolph has completed 64.2% of his passes for 6.6 yards per attempt with 30 touchdown and 22 interceptions. He's made 19 career starts, but has never established himself as an NFL starter.

    With their postseason hopes on the line against a stout Broncos defense, the Steelers are ready to give Rudolph another chance in favor of their aging future Hall of Famer.

    President Donald Trump remarked he would be willing to pardon reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if needed after Huang appears before Congress next week, according to an exclusive interview with the Newly introduced York Post.

    Sources indicate that huang's reinstatement followed Trump's intervention with Nvidia's board, including a reported call into a board meeting to argue for his return. Even so, lawmakers are still set to scrutinize his relationship with suspected Chinese intelligence asset Alice Huang in two appearances next week.

    Nvidia shares surged 31% on Monday after Huang was reinstated as CEO, before falling 5.9% on Tuesday amid a broader market pullback.

    "I expect him to take the Fifth Amendment so he doesn't incriminate himself in criminal prosecution, but we're going to give him a chance to explain," Kennedy said.

    Trump also told the Newly introduced York Post that he was open to the U.S. government taking an equity stake in Nvidia, similar to its stake in Intel in 2025, arguing that the company's success was vital to maintaining the U.S. lead in artificial intelligence.

    He also said it was his understanding that Huang had not had affairs with other women linked to Beijing and that he did not know how many affairs Huang had acknowledged.

    Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., the lead Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, told CNBC on Tuesday that he believed Trump was making decisions that could benefit his own stock portfolio, despite the president's assertion that he does not make trades himself.

    "If you don't believe that, you're too innocent to be let out of the house by yourself. The whole thing is a money-making operation. What's the alternative explanation?" Raskin mentioned.

    Separately, independent journalist Marisa Kabas reported that Huang told Nvidia employees at Tuesday's all-hands meeting that Trump "loves" the tech giant because of its employees' "contributions" to the U.S., while also addressing questions about whether Nvidia had become political or partisan.

    Industry observers note that "I want to be very clear: President Trump is the United States president. I'll do everything I can to help this president be informed about how he can make decisions in the best interests of the country," Huang noted.

    The reinstated CEO added that it would be a "great honor and a privilege" to go to Washington, D.C., to "inform them so the government can make the best possible decision," and said he would do the same for whoever becomes the next president.

    Recent findings suggest that "Don't think for a second politics played a role in the company. We are the most apolitical company. Everything he's done is because of his affection, admiration, and recognition of the great company that you are," Huang mentioned.

    U.S. jury convicts Huawei in a criminal trial over fraud and trade secrets

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (435 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Chinese technology giant Huawei was convicted Tuesday in Latest York on multiple federal criminal charges, including fraud, U.S.
    • The verdict marks a major development in a long-running criminal case against Huawei, with charges first publicly disclosed in 2019.
    • A federal jury found Huawei and three of its subsidiaries guilty of multiple offenses, including bank and wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering, the Justice Department remarked in a statement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Chinese technology giant Huawei was convicted Tuesday in Latest York on multiple federal criminal charges, including fraud, U.S. sanctions violations and conspiracy to steal trade secrets, following a three-month trial, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.

    The verdict marks a major development in a long-running criminal case against Huawei, with charges first publicly disclosed in 2019.

    A federal jury found Huawei and three of its subsidiaries guilty of multiple offenses, including bank and wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering, the Justice Department remarked in a statement.

    According to recent reports, "No person or company is above the law," U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche noted, accusing Huawei and its subsidiaries of conducting business in the United States through deception and theft.

    The Justice Department stated Huawei misrepresented its activities in Iran to banks to secure billions of dollars and retain access to U.S. dollar-clearing services. The company also supplied surveillance cameras that enabled Iranian authorities to monitor protests, the department said.

    Among the examples of intellectual property theft detailed by prosecutors were cases involving Cisco and T-Mobile.

    Huawei copied source code used in Cisco routers, with its engineers referring to Cisco by spelling its name backward in an attempt to conceal the theft.

    Huawei employees also sent photographs and technical details of T-Mobile's touchscreen-testing robot to China, with one employee later removing a component from T-Mobile's laboratory in a backpack, according to the Justice Department.

    "For over two decades, Huawei built its global empire on a foundation of fraud, theft, and deception," said Assistant Attorney General Tysen A. Duva of the Justice Department's Criminal Division.

    Huawei pushed back against the verdict in a statement issued Wednesday, while welcoming its acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge.

    "We believe the government's remaining charges are equally without legal or factual merit," Huawei noted, adding that the five trade secret-related disputes cited by prosecutors had previously been resolved as civil matters.

    The firm remarked it would review the verdicts and take necessary legal action to defend its interests, while remaining focused on maintaining uninterrupted business operations and investing in research and development.

    In a recent development, huawei and its subsidiaries face potential financial penalties, including fines, forfeiture and restitution, with sentencing scheduled for Sept. 14, 2027, according to the Justice Department.

    According to recent reports, U.S. prosecutors first publicly disclosed criminal charges against Huawei in January 2019, a month after the manufacturer's chief financial officer, Meng Wanzhou, was arrested in Canada.

    It has been revealed that meng returned to China in September 2021 after entering into a deferred prosecution agreement with U.S. prosecutors.

    It has been revealed that ahead of that matchup, the Steelers made headlines by reportedly benching veteran quarterback and former MVP Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph for Week 12 after recent struggles on offense. Rodgers will be inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, per Steelers spokesman Burt Lauten.

    In a recent development, we're watching plenty of injuries ahead of the action, including Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III, who's missed the last two games with a groin injury suffered in practice. He was officially limited on Tuesday. Fantasy football managers will also be keeping a Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers, who missed Week 11 with an ankle injury, though he was reportedly pushing to play in that matchup.

    The week also saw two players hit free agency after clearing waivers, including former Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones and former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk. Aiyuk reportedly has a visit scheduled with the Washington Commanders on Wednesday, who are short on receiver help after a season-ending knee injury to Terry McLaurin, while Jones' future remains up in the air.

    The Pittsburgh Steelers revealed Tuesday night that Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback on Friday against the Denver Broncos.

    Aaron Rodgers will be inactive.

    The injury report did note that it was just a walkthrough, but yesterday, when Philly did not practice, the team listed Barkley as a limited practice participant due to a neck injury as well as an illness.

    The Eagles play the Cowboys on Thursday afternoon for Thanksgiving.

    Brandon Aiyuk may have a new home sooner than later.

    Sources indicate that the former 49ers receiver is scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders. That's according to his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, who told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Aiyuk will meet with the Commanders on Wednesday.

    Ayiuk cleared waivers on Tuesday after previously being released by the 49ers, concluding a protracted and contentious breakup with the franchise.

    After finally being released by the San Francisco 49ers, veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has cleared waivers, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter, who also reported Tuesday that Aiyuk would like to sign with a upcoming team soon.

    He's expected to attract interest from a few teams, including the Washington Commanders, per Schefter.

    It has been revealed that the Niners releasing Aiyuk marked the end of a months-long standoff between the team and player.     Running back Josh Jacobs is also "questionable" for the Thanksgiving Eve game at SoFi Stadium.

    He's been recovering from surgery on the ring finger he fractured.

    The Kansas City Chiefs have been cautious handling the groin injury that running back Kenneth Walker III is navigating.

    Walker hasn't played since Nov. 8, a Week 9 win over the New York Jets.

    Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters that Walker will return to practice Tuesday.

    Recent findings suggest that "We'll see how he does," Reid stated, per Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. "I'm not anticipating a ton of work there, but he'll get out there and move around.".

    The Chiefs will travel to Buffalo this week for a Thanksgiving showdown with the Bills.

    According to recent reports, if there's anything that can slow this 49ers team, it's the blue medical tent. Injuries have ravaged the 49ers all season, and on Sunday night, San Francisco ran out a Geriatric Avengers of thirty-somethings including George Kittle, Mike Evans, Christian McCaffrey, Deebo Samuel Sr. and Kyle Juszczyk. All that experience gives the 49ers a major-game-pressure edge that few teams can match, but it also makes them intensely vulnerable to injury. Stints on the IR are a when, not an if, for the 49ers. Right tackle Colton McKivitz was the latest as he suffered a gruesome leg injury in the first half Sunday night.

    It has been revealed that the guy ensuring all those uncs get the ball is finally receiving some attention of his own again, too. Brock Purdy hasn't shown up on MVP leaderboards since finishing fourth in his breakout season of 2023. This season ought to change that. He's among the league leaders in touchdowns, passer rating and completion percentage, among other useful stats.

    Against the best defense in the NFL, all Purdy did was throw for three touchdowns and 255 yards on 21-of-26 completions. He's grown into the perfect weapon for head coach Kyle Shanahan's unorthodox offense, and Sunday was the perfect showcase.

    McCarthy was asked on Monday whether he was considering a quarterback change after the offense's poor play in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

    McCarthy kept it short and to the point, saying, "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback.".

    Pittsburgh dropped to 6-4 after the loss and fell to third place in the AFC North, trailing both the Cincinnati Bengals and the Cleveland Browns.

    The Steelers had 255 yards of offense but couldn't beat the Eagles. Philadelphia's win ended a seven-game losing streak for the franchise, and the Steelers have now lost two straight games, both coming after their Week 9 bye.

    In the loss, Rodgers was 30-of-44 passing for 227 yards and a touchdown. He led the team in rushing with 29 yards on five carries, but was sacked five times.

    If the Fresh England Patriots are interested in adding quarterback Daniel Jones, head coach Mike Vrabel isn't saying so.

    While Jones has cleared waivers, the Patriots named Tommy DeVito as their starting QB for Week 12's matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers. However, even if New England signed Jones, he would be unlikely to take the field with them so soon after joining the team.

    Taking over after Drake Maye was injured in Week 10's game versus the Detroit Lions, DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception. Vrabel said he was impressed by the backup QB's performance and the improvement he's shown since training camp, even if the Patriots didn't win the game.

    The plan is for Sam Darnold to start against the 49ers on Sunday, but Mike Macdonald wants to see the quarterback in practice first before making a final decision.

    Darnold has been out for two games due to a quad injury suffered in Week 8.

    Before Week 11, the Upcoming York Giants had a perception problem.

    They hadn't beaten a team with a winning record. Their advanced metrics remarked they were a below-average team. Their point differential was +7, which was meager for a 5-3-1 team. They looked like a team lucky to be playing in the putrid NFC East.

    Then on Sunday, the Giants got a win that can help legitimize their start. They beat a Jaguars team that was a major buyer at the trade deadline and looked like one of the NFL's elite teams. It was easily the Giants' biggest win this season, and for a team that has missed the playoffs eight of the past nine seasons, one of their biggest victories in many years. It might change what is being mentioned about the Giants.

    "We don't really worry about that, we don't really care what they think or what they say," Giants head coach John Harbaugh noted after the game, via the team's transcripts. "It's not our concern how we're evaluated. It's our concern how we play.".

    Yet, they knew what was being said about them.

    After missing nearly a year with tears to his ACL and meniscus, Micah Parsons is set to return to the Packers' defensive line this week. The star linebacker has reportedly been cleared to play as of Monday, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

    Parsons reportedly needed one final clearance on his knee before getting the green light, and will now make his debut against the Rams on Wednesday.

    New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome will be sidelined for "multiple weeks" with a high ankle sprain, head coach John Harbaugh confirmed on Monday.

    It's still unclear if Newsome will need surgery or if he will land on injured reserve, which would knock him out for at least four games.

    Sources indicate that "It's a serious high ankle. It's gonna be one of those lengthy high ankles," Harbaugh said, via ESPN. "It's going to be multiple weeks.".

    For more on Newsome's injury, click here.

    San Francisco is finally parting ways with wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk.

    Industry observers note that after a months-long saga around the receiver wanting to be released, Aiyuk was officially waived by the 49ers on Monday. That confirms reports earlier on Monday indicating that Aiyuk would finally be released.

    Other teams will have until Wednesday to claim Aiyuk, who will become a free agent after he clears waivers.

    Former Colts quarterback Daniel Jones was not claimed on Monday, thus making him a free agent.

    Jones is free to sign with any team that wants him, and that team can pay him the veteran minimum.

    The Colts still owe Jones about $20 million.

    The Commanders have activated running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt from injured reserve, and he is off the injury report.

    It has been revealed that JCM will play Monday night against the Bengals. He hasn't played since Week 5 due to a groin injury.

    So far this season, Croskey-Merritt has 239 yards and two touchdowns on 67 carries. He also has 40 yards on five receptions.

    The Cardinals have reportedly fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

    Sources indicate that arizona's defense has allowed 355.2 yards per game this season, the seventh-most in the league. The Cardinals' allowing 29.4 points per game is the second-most in the league, trailing only the Raiders at 29.7 points per game.

    San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch has agreed to a multi-year contract extension with the team, according to reports.

    Lynch and team owner Jed York agreed to the fresh contract with a handshake while on the sideline at Estadio Banorte before Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Fox Sports' Jay Glazer reported.

    Recent findings suggest that exact terms of Lynch's extension have not yet been reported. The 49ers have not officially revealed the agreement. Lynch's current contract was set to expire after this season.

    According to recent reports, lynch's new deal joins an extension for head coach Kyle Shanahan, who reached agreement on the contract in September shortly after the 49ers played the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia. San Francisco's international games this season have been extremely lucrative for the team's top football authority figures.

    Tech Report: As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • If Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    If Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the latest tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    It has been revealed that implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders significant and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," said Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Asian technology stocks tumbled Wednesday, led by a rout in Japanese semiconductor stocks, as renewed concerns over the artificial intelligence trade rattles investors following an overnight sell-off on Wall Street.
    • It has been revealed that japanese semiconductor stocks tied to the global AI supply chain were among the hardest hit.
    • Technology-focused investor SoftBank Group shed 15%, while semiconductor inspection equipment maker Lasertec lost 11.23%.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Asian technology stocks tumbled Wednesday, led by a rout in Japanese semiconductor stocks, as renewed concerns over the artificial intelligence trade rattles investors following an overnight sell-off on Wall Street.

    It has been revealed that japanese semiconductor stocks tied to the global AI supply chain were among the hardest hit. Advantest, a supplier of chip-testing equipment to Nvidia, plunged 13%. Tokyo Electron, which supplies chipmaking equipment to Nvidia's manufacturing partner TSMC, slumped 12.82%.

    Technology-focused investor SoftBank Group shed 15%, while semiconductor inspection equipment maker Lasertec lost 11.23%.

    Other Japanese chip stocks also came under heavy selling pressure, with Disco Corporation falling 9.41% and Renesas Electronics losing 9%.

    Tech stocks have seen heightened volatility over the past few months amid concerns over capital expenditure, skepticism over return on investments, circular AI financing, with Jensen Huang's ouster as Nvidia CEO adding fresh worries, and his return sparking a massive rally.

    Rolf Bulk, an analyst at The Futurum Group, said the renewed sell-off largely reflects lingering concerns over the sustainability of AI spending beyond 2027, with Huang's return doing little to fundamentally alter the outlook.

    "There are still concerns on the sustainability of AI demand, ability of the sector to finance the build-out, and questions around power supply," Bulk mentioned, adding that Japanese chip equipment makers were particularly vulnerable to a potential slowdown in AI infrastructure spending, given the highly cyclical nature of their business.

    It has been revealed that spending on wafer fabrication equipment could decline materially if AI demand slows from 2028 onward, Bulk said. South Korean memory chipmakers, by contrast, could be relatively insulated due to supply shortages.

    The country's memory chip giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, however, plunged more than 8%. The two are key suppliers of the high-bandwidth memory chips used in AI accelerators. Other South Korean technology stocks also traded lower, with LG Innotek shedding 5%.

    While the memory industry is also cyclical, Bulk expects shortages to intensify over the next two years, making a return to equilibrium between supply and demand in 2028 unlikely.

    In Taiwan, shares TSMC tumbled 7%, while Hon Hai Precision Industry plunged 8.6%. Electronic components maker Foxconn Technology shed 4.93%.

    Industry observers note that some Chinese technology stocks listed in Hong Kong bucked the broader regional sell-off, with Xiaomi jumping 4.6%, Kuaishou gaining 2.8% and Alibaba adding 0.7%. Tencent was marginally higher, while Meituan and Baidu was up 0.31% and 0.16% respectively.

    U.S. technology stocks fell overnight with the Nasdaq Composite giving back some of the sharp gains from the previous session that were fueled by Huang's return as Nvidia CEO.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Startup talent that has concentrated in artificial intelligence will return to the crypto industry "when AI implodes," according to Arthur Hayes, chief investment officer at Maelstrom Fund.
    • "A lot of talent has gone into the AI space, so I definitely think there'll be a resurgence in good founder talent coming back to crypto," Hayes said in an online interview with CNBC on Tuesday.
    • He added that some founders may also return once they "recognize" that their products could eventually be "usurped by Anthropic or OpenAI.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Startup talent that has concentrated in artificial intelligence will return to the crypto industry "when AI implodes," according to Arthur Hayes, chief investment officer at Maelstrom Fund.

    "A lot of talent has gone into the AI space, so I definitely think there'll be a resurgence in good founder talent coming back to crypto," Hayes said in an online interview with CNBC on Tuesday.

    He added that some founders may also return once they "recognize" that their products could eventually be "usurped by Anthropic or OpenAI.".

    The scale and capabilities of the largest frontier AI labs have made it difficult to "build a real AI business," Hayes said, arguing that "most" founders simply "raise a bunch of money and then light it on fire.".

    He expects the AI trade to face "serious headwinds" in the second half of 2027, when leading labs begin confronting sizable bills tied to compute leases and other non-cancelable commitments.

    Anthropic expects about $451.6 billion in compute and infrastructure obligations through the end of 2030, with roughly $70.7 billion due by the end of September 2027, according to its prospectus.

    According to recent reports, "Do they have the money? We're going to find out," Hayes said.

    According to recent reports, broader enthusiasm around the AI trade has also cooled amid questions about future infrastructure spending. Even exuberance from Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO on Monday proved short-lived, with the shares falling 5.9% on Tuesday and Anthropic dropping below its IPO price four days after its debut.

    In a recent development, the co-founder of now-shuttered crypto exchange BitMEX also thinks bitcoin could test $50,000 if the Nasdaq continues to fall. The cryptocurrency has shown little sign of recovery after dropping as low as $55,142.16 on Saturday — its lowest level since July.

    Bitcoin hit an all-time high of $126,279.63 in October last year and traded as high as $97,915.90 in January this year.

    It has now fallen for seven straight weeks — only the third such streak in its history — with crypto exchange Bitfinex attributing the weakness to equity-market sentiment rather than interest-rate expectations.

    In a recent development, hayes said he would like to see bitcoin rebound from around $55,000 even as the Nasdaq continues to fall. That divergence, he said, would suggest markets were shifting from a broad sell-off toward pricing in a "reflation" scenario, with the Federal Reserve eventually providing more liquidity.

    Neither bitcoin nor gold has yet decoupled from the Nasdaq, with Hayes describing the current market moves as a "correlation-led liquidation.".

    "Stuff goes down, you sell crypto first because it's easy, and then you sell everything else," he remarked.

    Once that pattern changes, Hayes remarked he would be interested in owning Zcash, which he described as a "high beta bitcoin" with a greater focus on privacy, as well as ENA, the token of Ethereum-based platform Ethena.

    Hayes mentioned a bitcoin rally could push up funding rates and futures-basis returns, increasing the income Ethena earns from its hedged crypto positions. That could make USDe, Ethena's synthetic dollar, more attractive and expand its circulation, he said, adding that he expects the ENA token to rise materially.

    "Those are the two things that I'm keeping an eye on, and when I'm ready to pull the trigger on buying risk again, those will be the things we buy a lot of," Hayes stated.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Treasury yields edged lower Wednesday as investors looked ahead to fresh inflation and spending data in a holiday-shortened trading week.
    • The 10-year Treasury note yield — the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — was 3 basis points lower at 4.8699%.
    • The yield on the 2-year Treasury note, which typically moves in line with short-term Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, was down more than 4 basis points at 4.6291%.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that U.S. Treasury yields edged lower Wednesday as investors looked ahead to fresh inflation and spending data in a holiday-shortened trading week.

    The 10-year Treasury note yield — the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — was 3 basis points lower at 4.8699%.

    The yield on the 2-year Treasury note, which typically moves in line with short-term Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, was down more than 4 basis points at 4.6291%.

    The longer-dated 30-year Treasury yield, which tends to track geopolitical events, was 2 basis points lower at 5.2695%.

    One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another.

    The dip comes after yields steadied on Tuesday, with traders digesting softer demand for a 5-year Treasury auction.

    With trading shortened this week due to the Thanksgiving holiday, investors are awaiting more data releases for clearer insights into the U.S. economic outlook.

    October's personal consumption expenditures price index — the Federal Reserve's preferred gauge of underlying inflation — is expected to remain unchanged month-over-month at 0.3%, according to economists polled by Dow Jones.

    Meanwhile, orders for U.S.-made durable goods in October — a measure of manufacturing activity and business spending — are forecast to rise to 0.2%, down from 1.8% in September.

    October's personal income and spending figures from the Bureau of Economic Analysis are also due.

    Bond markets will be closed all day Thursday for Thanksgiving, and will close at 2 p.m. E.T. on Friday.

    • He remarked the tourism industry was already picking up with occupancy rates returning to "almost near normal" and international carriers including British Airways and Air France rerouting flights to the UAE.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The UAE is "very optimistic" about achieving 7%-8% growth next year, the country's economy and tourism minister Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri told CNBC after the latest data from the International Monetary Fund demonstrated the country would avoid a recession in 2026.

    The IMF last week revised the UAE's real GDP forecast to 0.2% growth in 2026 from a 3.9% contraction predicted a month ago. "The UAE is coming back, and that adjustment within one month shows that there is a huge potential aspect when it comes towards the end of the year," the minister told CNBC's Dan Murphy.

    He remarked the tourism industry was already picking up with occupancy rates returning to "almost near normal" and international carriers including British Airways and Air France rerouting flights to the UAE. The minister expects economic growth to be higher than 0.2% this year.

    The Iran war has disrupted economic activity in the UAE, with missile and drone attacks from Tehran and maritime disruptions weighing on energy trade, tourism, aviation and private-sector confidence.

    According to recent reports, earlier this month, U.S. President Donald Trump remarked that renewed attacks on Iran were "highly unlikely" if negotiations produce a "very strong agreement." However, on Monday, Trump threatened that Tehran could face fresh U.S. strikes next year if the two countries failed to strike a deal, as per Fox News.

    "We can we cannot promise the world for any storms that will land on our shore, but we can always promise that the UAE's economy is ready for any storm," Al Marri said.

    He added that next year the UAE's economy will have a "different" model than the one before the conflict and investments will be focused on building factories and "things that we really need in times of crisis.".

    The World Bank in October said it expects the UAE's economy to recover next year, driven by rising oil production and exports and a rebound in tourism, trade, transportation, financial services, and construction.

    It warned that the improvement in economic activity in the UAE largely depends on the duration and intensity of the Iran war, with a faster de-escalation likely to accelerate the recovery in services exports and private-sector activity.

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    On platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    In a recent development, on Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note stated.

    Industry observers note that the Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    It has been revealed that in that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis hit Saudi Arabian sovereign wealth fund Public Investment Fund Tower on Tuesday, injuring 11.
    • Recent findings suggest that the kingdom's civil defense directorate did not name the tower, but posted an image showing damage to the PIF tower.
    • The injured included two Saudi citizens, two Indians, three Nepalis, and four Egyptians.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis hit Saudi Arabian sovereign wealth fund Public Investment Fund Tower on Tuesday, injuring 11.

    Recent findings suggest that the kingdom's civil defense directorate did not name the tower, but posted an image showing damage to the PIF tower. Eyewitness reports by Al Jazeera also indicated that the building that was hit was the PIF Tower in Riyadh.

    The injured included two Saudi citizens, two Indians, three Nepalis, and four Egyptians.

    The attack comes as tensions have flared up again between Saudi Arabia, which is leading an international coalition to restore the internationally recognized government of Yemen after it was forced to flee in 2015, and the Houthis.

    Turki al-Maliki, a spokesperson for the coalition, mentioned one of the towers of the financial center was targeted in a "cowardly terrorist attack," referring to the financial center in the Saudi capital of Riyadh.

    He added that authorities were conducting an on-site investigation at the scene of the attack.

    This has been the second attack by the Iran-backed group in six days on the tower, although the previous attack did not cause any casualties.

    On Wednesday, Houthi brigadier general Yahya Saree warned on X that the port of Jeddah and all Saudi ports along the Red Sea coast will become "targets for our forces," if Riyadh attacks the Yemeni Red Sea port of Hodeidah.

    According to recent reports, the coalition had asked civilians to evacuate the port "for their safety," on Nov. 20.

    In a recent development, attacks by the rebel Houthis have been escalating on Saudi Arabia, with the group targeting one of Saudi Arabia's oil refineries on Sunday, according to Reuters. The Houthis also rolled out drone and ballistic missiles against the country's airports, most recently targeting the King Khalid International Airport on Oct. 25, according to reports.

    According to recent reports, the upcoming attacks come amid wider strikes by Tehran and Iran-linked forces in the Gulf, with Bahrain also reporting that it was attacked by Iran over the weekend. Bahrain is home to the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet.

    "As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site," Bahrain's Ministry of Interior noted on X.

    The ministry later noted two people, a Bahraini citizen and a Pakistani resident, were injured in the attack.

    — CNBC's Azhar Sukri contributed to this report.

    #96378. Industry News: AI debt worries grow as Nvidia rebound masks Big Tech spending squeeze

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (761 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: AI debt worries grow as Nvidia rebound masks Big Tech spending squeeze

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (761 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Big Tech could find it increasingly tough to secure funding from debt markets critical to the AI build-out, as lenders become pickier over corporate bonds.
    • Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO on Monday gave an already-rising stock market a further lift, with tech shares leading a broad rebound on Wall Street after last week's sharp sell-off as Anthropic's landmark IPO failed to lift the broader sector.
    • But investors are now starting to ask harder questions about the bill for the AI build-out — and demanding evidence that the huge spending is actually adding value for shareholders, according to Dan Taylor, deputy chief investment officer and CIO equities, systematic at Man Group.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Big Tech could find it increasingly tough to secure funding from debt markets critical to the AI build-out, as lenders become pickier over corporate bonds.

    Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO on Monday gave an already-rising stock market a further lift, with tech shares leading a broad rebound on Wall Street after last week's sharp sell-off as Anthropic's landmark IPO failed to lift the broader sector.

    But investors are now starting to ask harder questions about the bill for the AI build-out — and demanding evidence that the huge spending is actually adding value for shareholders, according to Dan Taylor, deputy chief investment officer and CIO equities, systematic at Man Group.

    "As investors get choosier about where all this capital is going and when it might pay off, we think the market is likely to fragment well beyond the simple 'buy chipmakers, sell software' trade of the past two years," Taylor said.

    "Anthropic may have got its IPO out the door just in time, but for the rest of the AI trade, the era of spending first and asking questions later seems to be over.".

    Anthropic — which went public Nov. 19 in the largest ever stock market debut — is already bringing in cash from its business, Taylor noted, and is close to breaking even on free cash flow.

    It has been revealed that in contrast, heavy spenders and debt issuers — such as Oracle, Google owner Alphabet and certain chipmakers — plunged by 25-45% between their June peak and the market close on Friday, according to Man analysis. By comparison, Apple, which has sat out the AI spending arms race, was up almost 20%, Taylor observed in a Man Group note Tuesday.

    Nvidia closed about 5.9% lower on Tuesday. Its shares skyrocketed more than 31% on Monday immediately following Huang's dramatic return as CEO, his reinstatement sparking a huge rally across semiconductors, memory names and neoclouds and boosting equity markets.

    Matthew Rees, head of global bond strategies at L&G Asset Management, acknowledged bond markets have been consistently more bearish on Major Tech hyperscalers than equity markets. That stems partly from debt investors' broader outlook on the sector, but also from the sheer volume of issuance, Rees said.

    "You're seeing BBB names like Oracle and SpaceX that are trading more like single B, partly because of concerns over fundamental credit quality, but also very much concerns about supply," Rees told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" Tuesday.

    Sources indicate that accelerated AI-related borrowing is becoming a bigger share of U.S. corporate debt. PIMCO, citing Goldman Sachs data, expects the biggest AI companies to tap about $250 billion through bond sales this year. Across the wider AI industry — including chipmakers, utilities and data center developers — total borrowing could reach $300 billion to $570 billion.

    Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Alphabet are now on track to spend more on capital projects than their businesses generated in cash in both 2026 and 2027, according to Man Group analysis. Cole Smead, CEO and portfolio manager at Smead Capital Management, stated investors are now waking up to the risks of a spending boom that was leaving Big Tech companies — once the "largest cash generators in the world" — with less cash to buy back shares during sell-offs.

    "There are vast capital needs in this AI story. The only problem is there's just not enough money to go around," Smead said.

    He also questioned whether investors buying data center debt were being paid enough for the risks they were taking.

    "They think they're getting 200-300 basis points over 10-year Treasury," Smead told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" before Huang returned on Monday.

    "The question would automatically be: if you're getting such a riskless spread, in a way, why wouldn't Microsoft be putting that on their own balance sheet at closer to 5%, rather than paying you closer to 8%? The answer is because it's not riskless, and that's the matter here: people don't understand the risk they're taking.".

    Looking ahead, Taylor said the past week has demonstrated that a mega-IPO like Anthropic no longer lifts the whole market.

    According to recent reports, "We think the mega-cap tech spenders have room to rebound, yet doing so will likely require them to show more spending discipline and rebuild their free cash flow," Taylor said. "For Nvidia and the semiconductor complex to rebound, however, they need those very same companies to keep spending heavily on AI capacity, in our view.

    "It is hard to see how both sides get what they need at the same time.".

    NBA Cup 2026: Celtics avert disaster, Mavs roll listless Nuggets, Pistons deny Magic without Cade Cunningham

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1046 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Boston Celtics entered halftime of Tuesday's NBA Cup game apparently well on their way to snapping a four-game losing streak.
    • But it wasn't easy as they had to fend off a furious comeback effort from the Washington Wizards.
    • The Celtics opened an 80-49 lead at halftime that the Wizards cut to 117-112 in the final four minutes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Boston Celtics entered halftime of Tuesday's NBA Cup game apparently well on their way to snapping a four-game losing streak.

    They eventually got there. But it wasn't easy as they had to fend off a furious comeback effort from the Washington Wizards.

    The Celtics opened an 80-49 lead at halftime that the Wizards cut to 117-112 in the final four minutes. But the Celtics held on from there to avert disaster via a 131-116 victory.

    A Jayson Tatum 3 and two more by Baylor Scheierman in the game's final minutes helped ensure that the Celtics got back into the win column.

    In a recent development, with the win, the Celtics improved to 3-0 in NBA Cup play to maintain control of East Group C. The Wizards dropped to 2-2 in the NBA Cup.

    It has been revealed that tatum led the effort with 41 points, 8 assists and 6 rebounds. He shot 6 of 15 from 3, but made all of them before halftime as cold second-half 3-point shooting helped the Wizards mount their rally.

    Industry observers note that the Celtics were red-hot in the first half while shooting 15 of 26 (57.7%) from long distance. They shot 7 of 25 (28%) after halftime and needed three of those in the final minutes after the Wizards cut their deficit to five points.

    Ultimately, their 43.1% success rate from 3 was a cornerstone of their win, but questions will surely surface about the wisdom of continuing to hoist up 3s after building a 31-point lead.

    Paul George had no such struggles with a 28-point, 9-assist effort in which he shot 6 of 9 from 3. Anthony Davis led the Wizards with 33 points, 13 rebounds, 2 blocks and 1 steal.

    Cooper Flagg was the best player on the floor Tuesday night in a Mavericks win over the Nuggets.

    In a matchup of a former NBA champion and four-time MVP against a lineup featuring a rising NBA start, youth prevailed in Denver.

    Cooper Flagg and the Dallas Mavericks rolled a listless Nuggets team in Denver to the tune of a a 120-101 win.

    The Mavericks limited the Nuggets to 17 first-quarter points, then closed the second quarter with a 15-0 run to take a 58-39 lead into the break.

    The Nuggets answered with a 38-point third quarter and cut it as close as 80-77. But the Mavericks answered the run and closed the game strong to silence Ball Arena down the stretch with an overwhelming win.

    Flagg led seven Mavericks players in double figures with 24 points, a career-high 12 assists and 6 rebounds.

    In a recent development, jamal Murray countered with 20 points and 3 rebounds on a 6-of-17 shooting effort. Nikola Jokić had a relatively quiet scoring night with 18 points, 11 rebounds, 5 assists and 5 turnovers.

    Recent findings suggest that with the win, the Mavericks (10-7) improved to 3-0 in Cup play to take control of West Group A. The Nuggets (10-5) dropped to 2-1 in the NBA Cup to fall behind the Mavs.

    Cade Cunningham was a late scratch and watched Tuesday's Pistons win in street clothes.

    The Detroit Pistons secured an NBA Cup win over the Orlando Magic, but it was overshadowed by concern for Cade Cunningham, who was a late scratch due to a lingering knee injury.

    The Pistons played without their All-NBA guard and cruised to a 104-86 win to hand the Magic their first loss in NBA Cup play. The Pistons (11-6) are now 2-1 in Cup play, while the Magic (7-10) drop to 3-1. The loss blocked the Magic from from a chance to clinch East Group A.

    In a recent development, cunningham was listed as probable prior to the game due to lingering knee soreness. But he was a late scratch before an NBA Cup game, raising concern that his injury is one that could further linger.

    Industry observers note that head coach J.B. Bickerstaff declined to offer details on Cunningham's condition in his pregame news conference. He also didn't say much to tamp down concern.

    "He's battling through a lot, and I'll leave it at that," Bickerstaff said. "He's going to go out and compete and give us what he's got. But he's fighting through a lot.".

    It has been revealed that cunningham had previously missed one game this season, last Wednesday's 122-109 win over the New Orleans Pelicans. He struggled in his previous outing with a season-low five points in Sunday's 107-97 loss to the Atlanta Hawks.

    Industry observers note that detroit struggled to get its offense going early without Cunningham as the Magic jumped out to a 22-16 first-quarter lead on their home court. But the Pistons seized control with a 32-14 advantage in the second quarter and kept the Magic at bay from there.

    Recent findings suggest that isaiah Joe took Cunningham's place in the starting lineup and finished the game with a team-high 21 points alongside 4 rebounds and 1 steal. Daniss Jenkins was the primary playmaker in Cunningham's absence with 15 points and 10 assists. Desmond Bane led the Magic with 21 points and 5 assists.

    George is in the midst of a career renaissance in his first season with the Celtics.

    Recent findings suggest that wizards guard Kyshawn George learned the hard way Tuesday night. With the Celtics up massive in the second half, Paul sized up Kyshawn in isolation.

    He gained some separation with an arm extension on the perimeter, then crossed Kyshawn over as he drove to his right. Kyshawn did not stay with him.

    Instead, Kyshawn fell on his backside onto the court and into the legs of his teammate, Anthony Davis.

    It has been revealed that paul picked up his dribble and waited a beat while shooting a glance at Kyshawn — just to make sure Kyshawn was watching. Only then did Paul pull up for a jumper from just inside the 3-point arc that sank through the net to extend Boston's lead to 90-65 en route to its 15-point win.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, investors often favor dividend stocks for their regular income and the promise of potential share price appreciation. But selecting the right dividend stocks from a huge pool of companies can be difficult.

    Top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend-paying stocks, as their recommendations are backed by thorough analysis of a tech giant's financials.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    In a recent development, devon Energy (DVN), an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production firm, reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. The company announced a quarterly dividend of 32 cents per share for the fourth quarter, payable December 30. Based on the fixed dividends paid over the trailing 12 months, DVN yields 2.85%.

    Industry observers note that after hosting a virtual investor meeting with management, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Devon, with a price target of $59. Mehta said that he is now more confident in management's outlook for delivering strong near-term capital returns as well as efforts to drive operational efficiencies and productivity gains.

    Sources indicate that devon sees an opportunity to increase share repurchases, driven by solid free cash flow (FCF), contributions from the Eagle Ford divestiture and continued improvement in the balance sheet, Mehta remarked. Devon expects share buybacks worth more than $1 billion in Q4 2026, up from $414 million in the third quarter, backed by a strong pricing backdrop and improved capital efficiency.

    In a recent development, mehta, a 5-star analyst, said Devon expects about $6.3 billion of excess FCF in 2027, including about $3.5 billion of net proceeds from the Eagle Ford sale. That would enable the firm to accelerate buybacks while progressing toward its goal of reducing gross debt to about $9 billion by early 2027. Mehta noted that under DVN's framework to return up to 70% of annual FCF, management favors share buybacks as it believes the stock is discounted compared to large-cap peers.

    "Management expects continued capital efficiency gains from merger synergies, extended laterals, surfactant adoption and development of the newly acquired federal acreage," Mehta said.

    Mehta ranks No. 876 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 8.1%. See Devon Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    In a recent development, energy Transfer (ET), is a limited partnership that operates about 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. The organization recently unveiled third-quarter results showing net income per common unit growing about 18% year-over-year, to 33 cents. ET's cash distribution for Q3 2026 was 34.25 cents per common unit, up more than 3% year-over-year. At an annualized distribution of $1.37 per share, Energy Transfer yields more than 7%.

    Recent findings suggest that TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer with a price target of $25. The company delivered better-than-expected Q3 results and revealed the 1.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d) South Mississippi Pipeline, a 215-mile, 36-inch natural gas line linking the Perryville Hub to the Florida Gas Transmission (FGT) network, Gabelman stated. The project is supported by 20-year firm transportation agreements and is expected to enter service in 2030. ET expects to ultimately own 51% of the $1.6 billion project.

    The 5-star analyst said that Energy Transfer lowered its 2026 capital spending outlook to $5.5 billion (midpoint of the guidance range) from $5.75 billion due to project timing. Energy Transfer expects capex to rise to $7 billion in 2027, while Gabelman projects $5 billion in both 2028 and 2029, based on disclosed projects.

    Recent findings suggest that gabelman also highlighted management's commentary about optimization initiatives contributing an incremental $800 million to 2026 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, a larger benefit than in recent years. "A return to less commodity volatility should the [Middle East] war end could bring some relative downside, though this is offset by continued strong growth prospects," he said.

    According to recent reports, gabelman ranks No. 397 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15.4%. See Energy Transfer KPIs on TipRanks.

    Oil and gas exploration and production organization ConocoPhillips (COP) delivered better-than-expected Q3 performance. The company announced an 11% hike in its quarterly dividend to 93 cents per share, effective with the Q4 dividend payable on December 1. Based on the dividends paid over the trailing 12 months, COP yields about 2.6%.

    According to recent reports, following the Q3 results, Wells Fargo analyst Sam Margolin repeated a buy rating on ConocoPhillips, citing strong potential for further dividend increases. Margolin also trimmed his price target to $185 from $189 to reflect timing effects and the WAHA forward curve, though he said that COP could still re-rate as its natural portfolio lifecycle provides stronger protection against inflationary pressures than peers. The Waha forward curve tracks future natural gas prices based on the West Texas Waha hub.

    Margolin, another 5-star analyst, highlighted that ConocoPhillips' Q3 2026 adjusted earnings per share of $3.27 was well above Wells Fargo and the Street's estimates of $3.04 and $3.05, respectively. Earnings were driven by solid price realizations, partially offset by higher depletion, depreciation and amortization and purchased commodities.

    It has been revealed that margolin also noted COP's dividend increase and mentioned the accelerated buyback enabled by current commodity prices could further support long-term dividend growth. He sees the possibility of ConocoPhillips' dividend growth rate exceeding its current 6% cost of equity into the end of the decade. Margolin expects COP to sustain an 8% dividend compound annual growth rate through 2029 while repurchasing $6.4 billion of stock annually, and reducing net debt-to-capital to less than 9% by the end of 2028 based on the assumption of an average Brent crude oil price of $75 a barrel.

    "The message on the 3Q call was similar to that of 2Q, reiterating the moderation in reinvestment rate and commitment to dividend growth through the Willow start-up and after," Margolin stated.

    According to recent reports, margolin ranks No. 189 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 69% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.6%. See ConocoPhillips Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1789 w)
