    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    The biggest money-making energy trade looks over. What to buy instead

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Is one of the greatest money-making trades of the last few years coming to an end?
    • No, I'm not talking about Nvidia or any of the data center- or AI-related power companies (although they have been crushed lately too… more on that on CNBC TV.
    • I'm talking about whether the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    What I'm hearing from energy insiders.

    Is one of the greatest money-making trades of the last few years coming to an end?

    No, I'm not talking about Nvidia or any of the data center- or AI-related power companies (although they have been crushed lately too… more on that on CNBC TV. Tune in!).

    I'm talking about whether the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding. Over the last year, the jump in some of these companies has been nothing short of remarkable.

    That jump is largely due to massive increases in margins, earnings, and cash flow. Those have occurred because of a major jump in what is called a crack spread. That is the difference between the price of oil and the finished price of refined products such as diesel and jet fuel. For most of this year, spreads have been soaring as disruptions and attacks on facilities and shipping in the Arabian Gulf, Hormuz, and deep inside Russia have played havoc with the market. In the last week or so, however, something big has changed: many of those spreads have started to tighten.

    This seismic drop in spreads is causing a selloff in the aforementioned refinery companies.

    According to recent reports, if spreads continue to fall, these stocks may well keep selling off from recent highs. The upshot for investors may be that, as the shares come down, analysts see more upside. The median price target for Phillips 66 (PSX) now indicates a 20% gain from here, while smaller-cap Par Pacific (PARR) is double that.

    Here are a few other key points to focus on heading into the Thanksgiving-shortened week.

    I like to keep politics as much at arm's length as possible — we all know that energy and politics (sadly) often go hand in hand. Energy policies coming from Washington, D.C., can drive — or destroy — investment dollars. With all the big shifts in the White House over the last 10 years (four years of Trump, four years of Biden, and now 2 years into Trump #2), energy policies can blow through Washington faster than a summer squall hits a wind turbine. But because federal policies can mean so much for specific companies, sectors, and investments, it's important to follow the news flow.

    According to recent reports, that remarked, I'd like to take a moment to introduce you to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, known as BAAJA (and pronounced like the state in Mexico). Like much legislation, BAAJA is an obscure but vital bill working its way through the American Congress. BAAJA does a lot of things, but what Power Insider readers care about is its focus on energy permitting reform. In a nutshell, BAAJA would help speed up the building of newly introduced electricity infrastructure. Again, that's an overly simplistic view of a major bill, but it needs to be on your radar. The utility trade group Edison Electric Institute came out in favor of the legislation this month after the industry received some 11th-hour changes. See more about it in our recent interview with EEI President Drew Maloney here.

    In a recent development, the bill passed the U.S. Senate in a vote late Thursday night. Now it moves to the House. Support for its final passage is also coming from the big LNG trade group, whose executive director said he "applauds the Senate for its bipartisan effort to pass meaningful, bipartisan, and durable permitting reforms aimed at delivering greater predictability, consistency, and certainty in the permitting, production, and export process for U.S. LNG. This legislation moves us closer to untangling red tape and eliminating overlapping agency reviews that can keep U.S. energy projects delayed for years.".

    In a recent development, the Natural Gas Supply Association also chimed in, saying it urges Congress to see the bill as "a resource-agnostic and balanced reform agenda for boosting American energy security. It keeps strong environmental reviews in place, but it draws a firm line against the endless procedural delays that tie critical energy projects in knots for a decade.".

    In a recent development, in my view, passing BAAJA is an notable test of Congress's appetite for helping the energy and electrical power industry, lowering costs, and speeding time to market. The old adage was correct: time is money. Literally. If BAAJA moves on through the House, we could see an upside move in some utility stocks and any firm related to energy infrastructure.

    Sources indicate that speaking of politics, the news is getting lost in the massive Anthropic (ANT) IPO, but the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) — whose importance I wrote about in the last edition — just decided to resume permitting for data centers. The Texas Tribune did a nice write-up on it, and you can read it here.

    It's tough to say, but it's true. The two are inextricably linked by policies created at both the federal and state levels. As I wrote in the last edition, some federally elected officials may have less impact on state-level concerns — like the data center buildout — but they certainly have power over national laws. While many of you are enthralled, disgusted, or confused by sordid tales of Nvidia and Jensen-gate, keep one eye open on what happens in Washington, D.C.

    Have a great week, and have a wonderful Thanksgiving, everyone.

    Perhaps the big investor story — which is, like most things lately, related to Jensen-gate and Nvidia—is the sizable selloff in many AI, neocloud, and data center power-related stocks.

    According to recent reports, painful for current shareholders, but massive drops can also bring big opportunities. Wall Street believes that's the case, at least right now. Look at some of the potential upside based on the stocks' prices versus their price targets.

    In a recent development, we spoke with the CEO of Applied Digital (APLD) about all of this on CNBC last week, and you can watch it here. He highlighted how the market may be getting these stock stories wrong because, at least with his manufacturer, he has long-term contracts with solid-credit companies. In that way, Applied Digital is more like a landlord than a "pure-play" AI company.

    My take → While I'm not going to recommend a specific stock, I would add that it is critical for investors to understand the differences between these companies. While they may have some things in common, they are also different, with different business models, customers, leases, and sources of revenue.

    Speaking of recommendations… here are two ideas for you:.

    According to recent reports, A recent decline presents a nice opportunity in SOLV Energy (MWH). UBS analyst Jon Windham upgrades SOLV to buy from neutral, believing the market is "underappreciating several key tailwinds for SOLV given uncertainty around data center demand and higher interest rates." UBS highlights how the stock has fallen lately despite making two deals and beating and raising recent guidance. UBS says now is an "attractive entry point" for SOLV. (Side note: MWH is a great stock ticker.).

    While markets overall fall, BMO remains bullish on Bloom Energy (BE). After speaking with the firm, the analyst is upgrading Bloom to outperform, saying he remains "increasingly confident of BE's commercial traction" and that he still has conviction even with the recent drop in shares. While analyst Ameet Thakkar did cut his target to $230 from $260, that's still 50% upside from the current price. Bloom shares have tumbled 45% since October 1.

    Industry observers note that I was recently asked for my opinion on the price of oil. Here's my take. The market clearly wants to push oil contract prices lower and has for a few months. But, as I've said and reported for a while, don't confuse the futures (paper) price with the actual price. Yes, shipping rates and insurance rates have come down from recent highs — and there is a good amount of oil now flowing through Hormuz — but the cost of a physical barrel of crude is still well above the futures contract. If we get real, longer-lasting peace around Iran, oil prices will fall. There is plenty of oil in the world. That said, if bombs and missiles start firing again, oil prices will firm. I know that's a non-answer answer, but the oil market is truly headline-driven right now. My late good friend Boone Pickens (later in life, he didn't like being called by the "T" in his first name) used to avoid giving a set price target and instead give a directional quote, so I'll do the same: the odds of oil being lower in two months than it is today are 75%.

    Recent findings suggest that last week, I had a one-on-one with Vimal Kapur, chair and CEO of Honeywell International (HON), at an RBC conference in Newly introduced York City. While the conversation wasn't filmed, I can tell you that Kapur offered investors reassurance that his order book is doing very, very well. This is crucial because Honeywell is huge in the things that make other things work. Its sensors go into a ton of energy facilities, from refineries to LNG facilities. Honeywell is a leading indicator of spending and buildouts, so if it keeps getting orders, it's a good sign for macro energy.

    Bottom line: Watch Honeywell stock as a potential "tell.".

    Recent findings suggest that this week's Inside Line interview takes a different approach. We hit our friend Craig Johnson up for actionable insights into energy and stocks. Craig is managing director and chief market technician at Piper Sandler. He recently appeared on Power Lunch to talk about markets and stocks. He mentioned being bullish on energy, so we wanted to dig in just a little bit more.

    According to recent reports, this week, we had the pleasure of chatting with Balaji Krishnamurthy, president of Chevron Australia. We spoke at length about natural gas, the impact of disruptions, and long-term demand from Chevron customers in the Asia-Pacific region.

    Sources indicate that this is a bit of a local RBI for the Fresh York City area, but one I felt was notable to highlight. New York's electric grid operator just came out with a massive warning for everyone in our region: in just a couple of years, there may not be enough electricity supply to power our needs. A new report highlights a deficit in seven years, with a nearly 2 GW power hole in a decade. That's a number of major power plants' worth of energy. Get your solar panels on and buy that backup generator! I'll call this one random, but scary.

    Catch up with more on energy including interviews and video content from CNBC and Power Insider.

    #96351. Tech Report: Nvidia surge: What investors should do with the stock and the AI trade now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (787 w)

    AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Nvidia surge: What investors should do with the stock and the AI trade now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (787 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.
    • Investors and traders mentioned that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the company and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.
    • Industry observers note that "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you blink, you may have missed it.

    Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.

    Investors and traders mentioned that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the company and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.

    Industry observers note that "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday? Of course not, you can't be," mentioned Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, which counted Nvidia as its largest position as he bought on the dip over the last few weeks. "I'm trimming back.".

    "All the same complications that were here before Jensen resigned are still here," he added.

    It has been revealed that the day before Huang resigned on Nov. 12 as CEO, Nvidia closed at $173.73. It's intraday high on Monday was $171.50, up from its recent low around $125 as it was selling off in the wake controversies. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF closed at $506.96 the day before his resignation. It reached a high of $469.35 before losing steam as trading wore on Monday.

    Mike Khouw, YieldMax strategist at Tidal Financial Group, told CNBC on Monday that there were "sighs of relief," "applause" and even "cheering" among investors at the news of Huang's potential reinstatement. But he also mentioned there are still considerable risks facing the AI trade.

    Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang was not the only problem at Nvidia, he stated, and there are still many vulnerabilities in the overall AI trade, which should give investors pause. Credit-sensitive companies are still at risk of faltering, Khouw added.

    The national security implications of the scandal that has rocked Nvidia and the global AI trade more broadly aren't going away any time soon even as the Trump administration assured the Nvidia board there were none. Investors on Wall Street are expressing strategic concerns about ways to play the tech space just as lawmakers in Washington are demanding answers.

    Democrats are demanding answers on what exactly happened with Nvidia and the Chinese government.

    "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) said in a Monday statement. "The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement.".

    Industry observers note that house Ways and Means ranking member Richard Neal (D-Mass.) stressed the importance of Congressional oversight in determining the best course of action to move forward. The outcome of any Congressional investigations will likely be crucial for Nvidia's long-term viability as an investment opportunity, especially since the organization does so much international business.

    It has been revealed that "This is an export control matter," Neal told CNBC on Monday. "Congress is not subservient to this president or any other president as it relates to trade and tariff policies. This is a trade related issue.".

    Many of the same Democrats will call for a slowdown in the data center buildout, a strong problem for the public partly responsible for their Blue Wave earlier this month.

    It has been revealed that "You're going to have to work your way through what these data center moratoriums all mean," remarked Niles. "Now I think the broader market keeps going but I am not as convinced on the move in the data-center centric names from here.".

    To be sure, many Wall Street analysts were rushing to upgrade Nvidia's stock on Monday after Huang's reinstatement. Most restored price targets well above $200 with one as high as $270. But many traders think the rebound may fail before getting back to those levels.

    Famed short seller Michael Burry, who made a boatload betting against Nvidia with put options as it cratered, told his Substack audience that he thinks the rebound here could be "outsized," especially with low volume in the market overall because of the Thanksgiving holiday this week.

    But he too sees the rally eventually losing steam.

    "Jensen being back without much more information might even restore NVDA to the high 100s," Burry wrote. "I won't short it on this information I have today until it gets closer to or maybe hurdles $200.".

    Paul George is in the midst of a career renaissance in his first season with the Boston Celtics.

    Washington Wizards guard Kyshawn George learned the hard way Tuesday night. With the Celtics leading in the second half of their NBA Cup matchup in Washington, Paul sized up Kyshawn in isolation.

    He gained some separation with an arm extension on the perimeter, then crossed Kyshawn over as he drove to his right. Kyshawn did not stay with him.

    Instead, Kyshawn fell on his backside on to the court and into the legs of his teammate, Anthony Davis.

    It has been revealed that paul picked up his dribble and waited a beat while shooting a glance at Kyshawn — just to make sure Kyshawn was watching. Only then did Paul pull up for a jumper from just inside the 3-point arc that sank through the net to extend Boston's lead to 90-65.

    George, 36, entered Tuesday's game doing an admirable job of making Celtics fans forget about Jaylen Brown, whom he was traded for. He delivered agains Tuesday night with 28 points, 9 assists and 4 rebounds while shooting 6 of 9 from 3 as the Celtics held off a late Wizards rally for a 131-116 win.

    Recent findings suggest that george entered Tuesday averageing 19.9 points, 5.6 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 2.2 steals as the clear No. 2 option behind Jayson Tatum. He remains one of the game's best shooters with a 40.7% success rate from 3. And as Kyshawn learned Tuesday night, he's still got some moves.

    #96341. Kalshi daily volume of ‘perps’ trading begins to top its prediction markets

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (763 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Kalshi daily volume of ‘perps’ trading begins to top its prediction markets

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (763 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Kalshi is known for its prediction markets across sports, politics and culture.
    • But now, for the first time, perpetual futures, Kalshi's second financial product, has surpassed the notional trading volume of its event contracts on consecutive days.
    • Sources indicate that on Thursday, perpetual futures — commonly known as "perps" — on Kalshi saw $3.4 billion in notional volume as artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic stock debuted on public markets while the rest of the market sold off.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Kalshi is known for its prediction markets across sports, politics and culture.

    But now, for the first time, perpetual futures, Kalshi's second financial product, has surpassed the notional trading volume of its event contracts on consecutive days.

    Sources indicate that on Thursday, perpetual futures — commonly known as "perps" — on Kalshi saw $3.4 billion in notional volume as artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic stock debuted on public markets while the rest of the market sold off. That exceeded about $3 billion in notional volume for Kalshi's prediction markets on the same day.

    In a recent development, perps are futures-style contracts where there is no expiration and traders do not need to own the underlying asset. Contracts instead continuously track the price of an asset, with funding payments to keep the contract price aligned with that of the market. Funding payments are made periodically between holders of short or long positions.

    Sources indicate that perps trading surpassed event contracts one day in September, but on Friday perps topped prediction markets volume for a second day. Now Kalshi expects that performance to continue as it introduces perps tied to more individual stocks. On Monday, for example, Kalshi introduced contracts linked to Anthropic.

    Kalshi was the first to debut perps in the U.S. after winning federal regulatory approval in May to list perps tied to cryptocurrencies.

    Perps trading volume includes any leverage that speculators acquire along with their trade, while event contracts are fully collateralized — for now.

    Since the original launch in May, Kalshi has received approval to introduce perps tied to metals, crude oil, stock indexes and individual stocks.

    It has been revealed that offshore perps — those available on exchanges not regulated in the U.S. — generated more than $90 trillion in notional trading volume in 2025, so it's not surprising that the product has grown so rapidly on Kalshi, according to Udesh Jha, chief risk officer at Kalshi Klear, the organization's clearing house.

    "We're just in very early innings. We're launching products, we're growing the participant base.".

    Industry observers note that perps were Kalshi's first product to mark its transition from a prediction market-focused platform to a full-blown financial exchange where various assets are traded. Last week, reports said that Kalshi is planning to offer trading on equities on its platform in the coming months.

    At the same time, the company's perps product has come under fire. Some incumbent exchanges where futures are traded — which saw their stock prices decline following the approval of U.S. perps — believe the product was improperly approved. CME Group is suing the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal derivatives regulator, for approving perps.

    Recent findings suggest that others have simply expressed concerns about the efficiency of the markets. CNBC previously reported that trading volume on Kalshi's most popular perps markets — tied to bitcoin and ether cryptocurrencies — was dramatically greater than open interest, or cash actively in the markets. It's a phenomenon that isn't common with U.S.-regulated traditional futures, nor other offshore perps markets.

    Kalshi said at the time it has "zero concerns" about the distinction, and that it appears because less leverage is offered compared to offshore exchanges and there are fewer incentives for traders to park capital on its perps markets.

    While Kalshi started with cryptocurrencies, Owen Lau, an analyst at Clear Street, noted perps tied to individual stocks likely represent the most promising opportunity for growth in the U.S.

    "That's how I foresee the way perps will penetrate further into traditional asset classes," Lau said. "Perps on single stocks and [key performance indicators on individual companies] could change how investors hedge their portfolio or even make a directional bet.".

    According to recent reports, kalshi's growth has been powered by the fact that right now it's the only exchange that can actively list perps in the U.S., though crypto exchange Coinbase received approval in May to route U.S. users to offshore platforms for trading. That monopoly status, however, will probably prove short lived.

    Coinbase has filed to list single-stock perps in the U.S., and President Donald Trump in August noted the CFTC is working to bring Hyperliquid — a dominant player in offshore perps activity — to domestic traders.

    But Jha at Kalshi isn't worried about the competition.

    Sources indicate that "What will carry us is ... making sure that we have the right products for the marketplace, making sure we have the right surveillance of the products that we are trading.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    #96336. Industry News: Aaron Rodgers couldn't play forever, and he might have an unceremonious end at age 42

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (978 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Aaron Rodgers couldn't play forever, and he might have an unceremonious end at age 42

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (978 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Few players get the John Elway or Peyton Manning sendoff, winning a Super Bowl then announcing their retirement a few weeks or months later.
    • In a recent development, still, it seemed like Aaron Rodgers would have a gentler ending to his great career than a short statement at 11:10 p.m.
    • The Pittsburgh Steelers made a stunning move, announcing that not only would Rodgers be replaced as the team's starting quarterback for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, he wouldn't even be active for the game.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Few players get the John Elway or Peyton Manning sendoff, winning a Super Bowl then announcing their retirement a few weeks or months later.

    In a recent development, still, it seemed like Aaron Rodgers would have a gentler ending to his great career than a short statement at 11:10 p.m. on a Tuesday.

    The Pittsburgh Steelers made a stunning move, announcing that not only would Rodgers be replaced as the team's starting quarterback for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, he wouldn't even be active for the game.

    There were four MVPs, 10 Pro Bowls, a Super Bowl championship, dozens of highlights that defied belief over 22 seasons, and it all seems to end with a quick statement from the team after most of Pittsburgh had already gone to sleep.

    In a recent development, it's not like Rodgers has played great this season, which he noted will be his last in the NFL. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy was asked this week if Rodgers was still the team's starter, so it wasn't completely out of the blue that he got benched.

    Sources indicate that it was abrupt, and with some unusual timing. There was no time to celebrate the end of a legendary career or even realize that the snaps he took Sunday might be his last.

    It's just done, barring some other turn of events over the final few weeks of the season.

    Aaron Rodgers looks around during the national anthem before last week's game, which was the 267th of his NFL career. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images).

    Recent findings suggest that rodgers played OK this year. The Steelers couldn't have expected much more from a quarterback who will turn 43 on Dec. 2. No other quarterback, other than Tom Brady, had any reasonable level of success at Rodgers' age.

    Rodgers threw for 2,241 yards and 16 touchdowns with six interceptions in 10 games. The Steelers won six of those games and if the season ended now, they'd be in the playoffs. Rodgers wasn't great, often throwing short as he did last season, which was reflected in him having the fourth-worst EPA (expected points added) among all qualified quarterbacks. It still didn't seem like he'd be benched.

    It wasn't like the Steelers were giving the job to a hotshot rookie who will excite the fan base. Rudolph has been decent as a backup throughout his career, and he had a stretch in 2023 when the Steelers won all three of his starts that helped them to the playoffs. But the Steelers didn't feel any urgency to see what Rudolph can do. They just apparently felt Rodgers had already hit the age cliff and they saw it over the last two games.

    It has been revealed that after a solid start to the season there were two miserable performances from Rodgers and the team. He threw incomplete on his first seven passes in a blowout loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10. That was the first time in his career he had started 0-for-7. Pittsburgh's loss on Sunday in Philadelphia was ugly, with the Steelers not scoring a touchdown until the final two minutes. Undrafted rookie Max Hurleman, making his NFL debut, might have become a trivia answer: He caught the Steelers' only touchdown against the Eagles, and it might end up being the final touchdown pass of Rodgers' career. As it stands, that could be the final play of Rodgers' career. Pittsburgh never got the ball back after that.

    The Steelers were slumping. But the way the week unfolded makes the benching quite odd.

    Sources indicate that the Steelers have a short week. When asked Monday about Rodgers and possibly benching him, McCarthy gave a terse answer: "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback." Then less than 48 hours later, with a game less than three days away, the Steelers made a change at quarterback.

    It has been revealed that the benching likely happened before 11 p.m. on a Tuesday but that's when the NFL world found out, making it one of the odder quarterback announcements in recent memory. And the decision to demote Rodgers all the way to at least No. 3 on the depth chart (the Steelers are the rare team that carries four quarterbacks) was made by a coach with whom Rodgers won a Super Bowl with at the end of the 2010 season. There wasn't anything pleasant about the move or how it was handled, and an NFL legend like Rodgers probably deserved better. But the league isn't much on sentiment, especially for teams on two-game losing streaks in a playoff race.

    Maybe there will be more details to the benching, other than a coach who definitively stated Monday that Rodgers was his quarterback completely changing his mind on a Tuesday (a day when the Steelers had a walkthrough practice), three days before his team plays the 8-2 Broncos.

    Recent findings suggest that rodgers has spent most of his career, particularly the final few years of it, living in defiance. His confidence never wavered, whether talking about politics, criticizing the media or showing up teammates and even his coach on the field when he felt he wasn't at fault for a bad play. It never seemed he'd leave the game unless it was on his terms. Perhaps he gets a start later in the season if Rudolph doesn't play well or there are injuries or simply to give an all-time great a better sendoff than a social media blast late in the evening.

    Sources indicate that but there's a good chance we've suddenly seen the last of Rodgers on a football field, especially with the team making sure the world knew he wouldn't even be active Friday. The NFL can be a cold business, even for someone who was one of the faces of the league for a couple decades.

    #96333. AI debt markets shudder as Nvidia's top 'banker' returns

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (989 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    AI debt markets shudder as Nvidia's top 'banker' returns

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (989 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.
    • Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.
    • Huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.

    Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.

    Huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees. His return to Nvidia has revived prospects for the company to continue "circular financing" of AI chips and data centers — raising concerns among credit investors.

    It has been revealed that coreWeave, which has become the poster child of AI debt concerns, saw its stock sink 13% and the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 top 17%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    In a recent development, at the same time, the spread on the neocloud company's five-year credit default swaps jumped 8.5% to over 1,200 basis points. Credit default swaps are insurance against nonpayment and are considered a barometer of perceived risks. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.

    Industry observers note that huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after stepping down on Nov. 12 amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. His reinstatement on Monday was cheered by investors, who pushed stocks higher, yields lower and spreads on CDS tighter. However, stocks retreated, bond yields rose and CDS spreads widened on Tuesday.

    Ben Emons, founder and chief investment officer at FedWatch Advisors, called it a waning of the "Jensen effect.".

    The moves suggest "markets see government intervention as 'moral suasion' that carries credit and interest-rate risks," he mentioned.

    President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday he "convinced" the board to bring Huang back.

    Industry observers note that coreWeave wasn't the only name seeing heightened concerns in CDS spreads. Oracle's five-year CDS spread jumped 7% to 355.68. Even highly rated hyperscalers Meta Platforms and Amazon.com saw spreads widen by more than 2%. Nvidia's CDS added 3.4%.

    Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager for fixed income at Catalyst Funds, believes the drama that unfolded with Huang's return to Nvidia won't necessarily sit well with credit investors.

    "A lot of old school credit people are going to look at what kind of materialized there, the administration's involvement in putting him back in, and I think a lot of credit participants are going to step back and tiptoe away from that a bit," he remarked. "Credit market investors typically don't like that type of drama or uncertainty.".

    Sources indicate that while Nvidia has commitments across the AI ecosystem, it is the neoclouds that have been under the most scrutiny. Many of the companies, which rent out AI computing power and cloud capacity, are highly leveraged and have relied on Nvidia financing to reduce their exposure to the bond market.

    With so much riding on Nvidia's funding, Huang's next move is being closely watched.

    During his brief absence, chief financial officer Colette Kress mentioned during the manufacturer's earnings call that Nvidia would be "rigorously evaluating future investments" and will remain disciplined in how it commits capital.

    That suggested Nvidia was going to be more judicious with financing, states Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets.

    "That concern should be put to rest with Jensen [Huang] back," he noted.

    Investor Steve Eisman, of "Big Short" fame and host of "The Real Eisman Playbook" podcast, believes Huang feels emboldened now that he's back in charge.

    "[H]e'll double down on the circular financing," Eisman predicted on CNBC's "Squawk Box" Tuesday.

    After Huang's departure, Eisman believed that the ecosystem the CEO created by pouring money into AI companies would likely unwind and leave some of the companies in "substantial trouble.".

    "Now that he's back, they're not," he stated.

    Others are not so certain the level of funding will continue.

    It has been revealed that "Given scrutiny of disclosure around financing and guarantees … we do not expect Mr. Huang's return to bring a quick reversion to broader customer financing," Stifel analyst Ruben Roy said in a note Monday.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia said on its earnings call that it has $118 billion in guarantees, as of Oct. 25, to back AI projects.

    Concerns about the level of debt to fund the AI infrastructure buildout had already taken hold before Huang's departure and reinstatement.

    "These issues have not disappeared just because the White House pressured the weak board to reinstate Jensen Huang," mentioned economist David Rosenberg, founder and president of Rosenberg Research.

    John Lloyd, global head of multi-sector and corporate credit at Janus Henderson Investors, believes having Huang back at the helm "reaffirms his existing go-to-market strategy." However, the credit market is still taking a cautious look at the neoclouds as it waits for more clarity on long-term supply/demand dynamics.

    Still, Lloyd is cautiously positive on CoreWeave, which he owns in portfolios he manages, and noted all the data point to a "pretty healthy environment right now." That includes strong residual values on graphics processing units and spot compute rates, he noted.

    Recent findings suggest that "The organization is doing everything in its power to execute," he stated. "They don't need the high yield market at this time.".

    In a recent development, in the meantime, investigations into Nvidia and Huang are ramping up. Huang is expected to appear before three House committees next week. Nvidia is conducting an independent investigation into his activities, and California Attorney General Rob Bonta has introduced a probe. At the federal level, President Trump said Monday that U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    It has been revealed that "There's other shoes to drop," Rosenberg mentioned. "I don't think that the book has been closed on this file.".

    #96323. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

    📅 09 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3019 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot at the moment “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.
    • In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.
    • “We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot at the moment “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

    In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

    “We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

    In a recent development, “We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”.

    Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

    It has been revealed that alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

    A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

    Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

    Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw.

    It has been revealed that at that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

    Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

    It has been revealed that cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

    According to recent reports, liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré. Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88).

    They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

    Industry observers note that yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

    Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

    Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

    A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

    In a recent development, as usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

    Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

    Recent findings suggest that monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

    Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

    Industry observers note that konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

    Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

    It’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’.

    Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

    Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

    Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

    In a recent development, liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

    Sources indicate that monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

    It has been revealed that A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

    It has been revealed that quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

    Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

    It has been revealed that isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

    Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw.

    Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

    Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

    For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

    Much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

    Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

    Charlie Adam claims the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

    Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

    Industry observers note that the referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

    Liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

    A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

    Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

    Significant cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike.

    The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

    It has been revealed that liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

    Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

    Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

    It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

    In a recent development, liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

    Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

    Excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

    Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

    Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

    Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

    Tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

    In a recent development, liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

    A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe.

    Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

    According to recent reports, the crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

    Sources indicate that virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

    For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

    It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

    Sources indicate that I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

    Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

    But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

    I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

    I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

    Liverpool Alisson; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Szoboszlai, Gakpo; Koumaz, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak.

    Monaco Hradecky; Vanderson, Dier, Sané, Nazinho; Detourbet, Cabral, Camara, Golovin, Abline, Biereth.

    Eric Dier captains Monagesques:.

    Le 𝐗𝐈 qui débutera cette rencontre face à 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐨𝐥 📋 pic.twitter.com/2cOYRbzUEN.

    It has been revealed that 🥳 Feliz aniversário, 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐞 𝐋𝐮𝐢́𝐬! 🎉Notre coach fête aujourd'hui ses 41 ans 🎂 pic.twitter.com/VTd4BQ5rRK.

    Alisson, Van Dijk and Gakpo return, Ndukwe continues in defence.

    The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺.

    Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

    Industry observers note that this afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under upcoming management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

    According to recent reports, in pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

    Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

    Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

    Salvai calcia dalla distanza, palla fuori di pochissimo.

    Richiamato all'FVS il direttore di gara per possibile un fallo in area di rigore di Sciabica su Sarriegi.

    #96308. Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' WR Blueprint for Week 12

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 30m • 📚 Deep Dive (5932 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' WR Blueprint for Week 12

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5932 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can.
    • According to recent reports, it's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning.
    • Chase had a disappointing Week 11 in a good match.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be an RB column, this WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

    According to recent reports, it's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position will be updated here soon.

    1. Ja'Marr Chase (vs. NO) - 93.5 proj. receiving yards.

    Chase had a disappointing Week 11 in a good match. Some of that was not coming down with his deep target. Some of that was the rain. A lot of it was Joe Burrow having an off night against a chaotic defense. It happens. He's still the WR1 on WR4 usage this month and the WR4 across the year.

    It has been revealed that the Saints have done a decent job on underneath passes but have allowed others to win downfield. There's no reason for the Bengals to move off of their league-leading 67% neutral pass rate here. Cincy has a 30.25-point team total (second).

    In a recent development, 2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (at SF) - 97.5 proj. receiving yards.

    According to recent reports, smith-Njigba is the WR2 in per-game half PPR scoring on WR6 expected-points usage over his past four games with Drew Lock and Sam Darnold splitting time. He has topped 100 receiving yards in three of those four contests while drawing a 44% target share in that span. What's upcoming?

    Sources indicate that san Francisco ranks 11th in half PPR points allowed per game to opposing wideouts, having surrendered 71.2 fantasy points to the Cowboys receiver room in Week 10 when chasing points. JSN has tons of experience against this defense, most recently posting 118, 19, 84, 124 and 118 yards. Seattle travels as 3-point road underdogs with a 21.75-point team total (17th). Throwing the ball to the perimeter is the best way to move the ball against the Niners, in my opinion.

    In a recent development, 3. CeeDee Lamb (vs. PHI) - 89.5 proj. receiving yards.

    Lamb is the WR3 on WR2 usage this year, ranking second in targets per game (11.8) and third in yards per game (100.7). Through 11 weeks of an NFL season, Lamb's 208.2 half PPR points are 13th all-time. All-time.

    It has been revealed that the Eagles have been bad against Lamb-type receivers all year and now won't have All Pro LB Zack Baun. They've allowed the third-most points to fantasy WRs, and Lamb finished as the WR5 on WR1 overall usage against them in Week 7. Dallas carries a 28-point team total (fourth) as 8.5-point home favorites.

    4. Amon-Ra St. Brown (vs. CHI) - 84.5 proj. receiving yards.

    According to recent reports, st. Brown is having his usual season. He's the WR5 on WR7 usage, after going on a touchdown-less rut throughout October.

    Sources indicate that this matchup has the potential for a blowup game. The biggest factor will be if slot CB Kyler Gordon can play after he missed last week. The Bears have been pretty woeful in the secondary beyond him, while shutting down the run since Jeffery Simmons appeared. The Sun God was the WR5 and WR1 in matchups against them last year, both wins for Detroit. Jaxon Smith-Njigba hung 118-1 against them in Week 8 in a similar role, too. Detroit enters as 2.5-point home underdogs carrying a 26.5-point implied team total (sixth).

    According to recent reports, 5. Justin Jefferson (vs. ATL) - 84.5 proj. receiving yards.

    Industry observers note that jefferson is the WR18 on WR8 usage over the past two weeks with Kirk Cousins. The fumble on that in-cut explosion was a real bummer, but that completion had a lot of timing and anticipation from the QB, something Jefferson hasn't had since 2023. He had plenty of breaking routes against the 49ers, and Kevin O'Connell drew up two different downfield shots to him, too. A substantial game is long overdue. The signs of it happening soon are there.

    (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports).

    It has been revealed that this is a sweet matchup for just that. The Falcons don't have Pro Bowl FS Jessie Bates, and CB1 A.J. Terrell is having a down season in isolation. The Vikings getting their OL healthy again would be nice, but Jefferson should have room to operate either way. The Falcons have allowed the fifth-most passing yards per game this year and the seventh-most fantasy points to WRs. Minnesota has a strong 24.75-point team total, and Jordan Addison (finger) isn't expected to play.

    6. Parker Washington (vs. TEN) - 78.5 proj. receiving yards.

    It has been revealed that that really should've been a touchdown. Come on, refs! Washington still was a top-20 WR last week and is now the WR13 on WR12 usage across the season. He can be up-and-down based on the Jaguars' lopsided history, but when games are tighter, Washington catches fire, as he did last week when he racked up 16 targets while trailing.

    (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports).

    In a recent development, this week, the Jaguars are expected to go crazy on offense. They have a league-high 31.0-point team total against the Titans, who have allowed 362 passing yards per game over the past month. Read that again. And again. It's one of the wildest stats of the year. It doesn't take a genius to feel good about Washington's ceiling odds here. He had 152-1 against them just two weeks ago.

    7. Tee Higgins (vs. NO) - 70.5 proj. receiving yards.

    It has been revealed that higgins was only targeted three times in last week's disappointing upset loss. It happens at WR, even for the top options. Higgins' best games are likely behind him, but he is the WR7 on WR20 usage this year. His worst-case scenario is returning back to the WR1/2 border as the season closes. The schedule is light enough to dream higher than that.

    (Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports).

    It has been revealed that the Saints have allowed the fourth-most points on 15+ air yard targets to WRs. That's the clear upside path he needs in a rebound spot. The Bengals have a 30.25-point team total (second).

    8. George Pickens (vs. PHI) - 70.5 proj. receiving yards.

    We're so back. Pickens has 38.0 and 20.3 half PPR points, respectively, in his two games since the bye. He had one of the best grabs of the year last week along the sideline, while Dak Prescott had all day to pass behind a great Cowboys OL. It's an environment for Pickens to have monster games, even if his role and style come with some volatility. He's at his best when teams go to single high coverage, something the Eagles typically don't do.

    In a recent development, that said, CB1 Quinyon Mitchell is dealing with a newly introduced hamstring injury, and the other star players won't be available with Jordan Davis on the Jaguars and LB Zack Baun on IR. Mitchell's status is a substantial deal for Pickens' matchup. Across the season, the Eagles have had far too many blown coverages, leading to the third-most fantasy points allowed to WRs (31.3). Pickens had 57-1 against them in Week 7 and 146-1 against them late last year. Dallas carries a 28-point team total (fourth) as 8.5-point home favorites.

    9. Malik Nabers (at IND) - 64.5 proj. receiving yards.

    In a recent development, nabers had a handful of underneath receptions against elite CB1 Travis Hunter last week, then teleported into the back of the end zone against Jacksonville's nickel defender to bring Nabers to a top-15 WR finish. Since Week 4, Nabers is the WR9 on WR4 usage with Puka Nacua as one of the receivers ahead. Things will always be up-and-down with J.J. McCarthy, who missed him way out of bounds for a potential back-shoulder TD, but Nabers is way too good to not be treated as a fantasy WR1 now.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.
    • The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.
    • Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

    The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

    Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

    But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

    The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

    Industry observers note that ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

    Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

    Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

    When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

    The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

    Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

    Industry observers note that yesterday Arsenal revealed the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:.

    According to recent reports, “I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a upcoming challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

    Industry observers note that “I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”.

    Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

    Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

    “I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

    It has been revealed that “I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”.

    This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

    Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

    If Aaron Rodgers is done for the season, why are Steelers rolling with Mason Rudolph?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Standing just past the end zone of the Pittsburgh Steelers' training camp field on an August afternoon, Will Howard reflected on his offseason.
    • He'd dropped from 242 pounds to 230, he remarked.
    • "I feel like it's been a long time since I've actually played real football," Howard told Yahoo Sports on Aug.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Standing just past the end zone of the Pittsburgh Steelers' training camp field on an August afternoon, Will Howard reflected on his offseason.

    He'd dropped from 242 pounds to 230, he remarked. He wasn't battling the bone fracture on his hand that had slowed his rookie year. He was a year into learning his personnel, even if he was newer to head coach Mike McCarthy's offensive system. The Steelers' 2025 sixth-round pick admitted he was excited.

    "I feel like it's been a long time since I've actually played real football," Howard told Yahoo Sports on Aug. 4. "And I think there's a lot of excitement around the Steelers and around, I feel like, me a little bit.".

    Howard appreciated the energy from fans flocking to training camp headquarters in Latrobe, Pennsylvania. But the Ohio State product was also realistic about buzz around the Steelers' younger quarterbacks.

    "Makes me feel great, but at the same time, it's all anticipatory," Howard noted. "I haven't really given them anything to truly cheer about. So I want to actually go out there and improve myself this year and give them something to really cheer about.".

    After Tuesday night's stunning benching of Aaron Rodgers, could that materialize?

    The Steelers announced at 11:10 p.m. local time Tuesday that 31-year-old Mason Rudolph would be the starting quarterback for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos.

    "Aaron Rodgers," they added, "will be inactive for the game on Friday.".

    The primary oddity lies in the Steelers' current decision, which feels sudden and strangely timed on a short week to prepare for a complex Broncos defense.

    But there also remains the questions facing Pittsburgh's medium- to long-term future: How do the Steelers weigh their playoff contention this year against their quarterback outlook longer term?

    It shouldn't surprise anyone that head coach Mike McCarthy would rather call plays for Rudolph, who has 38 games of NFL experience, including 19 starts, compared to Howard and Drew Allar at zero. Right now, the 6-4 Steelers sit seventh in the AFC with the final wild-card spot.

    In a recent development, the 5-5 Upcoming England Patriots lost quarterback Drake Maye this season and, seemingly, their playoff promise with it. The 4-6 Houston Texans loom below New England — and also loom on the Steelers' schedule after the Broncos.

    The Steelers need a quarterback who can keep receiver DK Metcalf in check, spark their run game and overcome protection deficits.

    It has been revealed that perhaps Rudolph starts at least until that Sunday primetime game vs. Houston in Week 13, while playoff hopes live. And perhaps Pittsburgh's postseason outlook is rosier than its recent play in losses to the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles, given the relatively shallow state of the AFC compared to the NFC.

    Either way, general manager Omar Khan may need to ask himself: How long should I chase a roster on track for a first-round playoff exit, rather than build a roster that's set up to threaten for years to come?

    McCarthy waxed poetic at training camp about how much his younger quarterbacks were learning in meetings from Rodgers' reflections on footwork, reads and plays in this offensive system.

    The Steelers' closest taste so far this year was in the preseason with Howard, Allar (a 2026 third-round draft pick) and Rudolph.

    Their surrounding casts varied. But across three preseason games, Allar completed 55.6% of pass attempts for 351 yards and two touchdowns and Howard completed 66.7% for 229 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. Allar also rushed for a touchdown.

    In one preseason game, Rudolph went 10-for-11 passing for 93 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions.

    Rudolph was named Rodgers' backup when the 53-man roster came down.

    But the question remained: Would the Steelers reach a point in their season when they want to evaluate the room more broadly before deciding how to approach the 2027 draft?

    Rodgers had stated clearly that this is his last season. He was, at season's start, the Steelers' present but not their future.

    I had serious reservations about the Mike Babcock hire -- and I still do -- but Edmonton has been mauling opponents early. The Oilers are off to a 5-0-1 start while posting a plus-11 goal differential. Each of the team's wins has come by at least two goals.

The most impressive part of Bouchard's game to this point has been his five-on-five impacts. With Bouchard on the ice, the Oilers have outscored opponents 15-2, per Natural Stat Trick.

    With Zach Hyman and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins out of the lineup, the Oilers haven't missed a beat thanks to its trio of superstars.

    As the Oilers challenge the defending champs for the No. 1 spot, here are the updated NHL Power Rankings.
